newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibia's Swapo accused of stirring tribal conflict.
newsitem.headline: Namibia's Swapo accused of stirring tribal conflict.

text.p: The DTA of Namibia, the southern African country's official opposition in parliament, on Wednesday accused President Sam Nujoma's ruling Swapo party of stirring tribal conflict.
"Namibia is rapidly becoming a dictatorship in which those who oppose Swapo will enjoy no civil or political rights," DTA President Mishake Muyongo said at a news conference.

"Swapo is clearly bent on creating tribal conflict in Namibia when one looks at the way in which this party has been applying double standards to the ordinary people of Namibia in contrast to its own supporters," he said.
Warning that this practice had led to most of Africa's civil wars, the DTA pointed to the weekend disruption of a scheduled inauguration of the king of the OvaZemba tribe.

The party also pointed to the police's breaking-up of a recent meeting by Himba opposed to a planned hydro-electric scheme, and their action against San demonstrators near the Etosha National Park last year.
The OvaZemba, a Herero tribe numbering between 5,000-10,000, fled Angola in 1945 to escape oppression by Portuguese settlers.
They settled near Ruacana and were made to fall under the authority of the Aakolonkadhi, an Ovambo tribe, by the then South African administration.

Under the Traditional Authorities Bill of 1995, which provides for communities of a certain size, equal language and culture to be headed by their own traditional leader, the OvaZemba decided to revive their own clan.
Police said Saturday's inauguration ceremony was illegal in terms of President Sam Nujoma's decree last month that no public gatherings would be allowed without written police approval.

The inauguration had apparently also not been sanctioned by Local Government Minister Nickey Iyambo. But the DTA said that this year alone, two other inaugurations of traditional leaders had taken place with Swapo's blessing.
